title: VS Code MCP inputs and agent-originated commands can execute unexpected local commands
summary: MCP notification links and install-link variables can execute commands. Unvalidated legacy SSE endpoints can redirect requests and expose credentials. Agent-originated local-command syntax can also bypass expected terminal approval.

severity.rationale: A malicious MCP server or prompt content can reach local commands and credentials under common integration prerequisites. Connection, click or tool-approval requirements limit reach; act within 72 hours.

affected.note: All four advisories list versions before 1.145.3.

exposure: Elicitation needs a connected hostile server and a notification-link click. Install links need installation approval. SSE needs connection to a hostile server. The Agent Host path needs attacker-influenced child prompts and a granted related session tool operation.

params.instructions: Check the actual VS Code installation version, including installations whose code command is absent from PATH. This record does not establish applicability to forks.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Upgrade VS Code to 1.145.3 or later. Connect only to trusted MCP servers and avoid untrusted install links and notification links. Until patched, remove affected SSE servers; prefer the Copilot harness to the Local harness and avoid session-wide tool grants for untrusted instructions.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updating and restarting can interrupt dependent workflows.

verification: Confirm the installed version and the component used by running processes meet the documented fix or containment condition.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
